results.query: Which diagram illustrates theoretical throat, effective throat, and actual throat, and how are they defined in Clause 4?
results.answer: In Figure B25 (Weld Sizes, printed p. 123, PDF index 135) of AWS A3.0M/A3.0:2020, fillet weld throat dimensions are illustrated: theoretical throat is the distance from the beginning of the joint root perpendicular to the hypotenuse of the largest right triangle inscribed within the fillet weld cross section; effective throat is the minimum distance minus any convexity between the fillet weld face and the weld root; and actual throat is the shortest distance between the weld root and the face of a fillet weld.

results.slice_name: Slice 2 — 3-Tier Compound Designations & Invalid Variant Rejection
results.query: Explain why OFC-A-MA is a valid designation while FCAW-Z-SA and PAW-AU-ME are rejected in AWS A3.0.
results.answer: In AWS A3.0M/A3.0:2020, OFC-A-MA is a valid compound designation for manual oxyacetylene cutting (combining Table A1 base process oxyfuel gas cutting with Table A4 application mode). In contrast, other proposed combinations are not in the standard: FCAW-Z-SA is rejected because Process variation 'FCAW-Z' is not a standardized process variation of 'FCAW' in AWS A3.0M/A3.0:2020. PAW-AU-ME is rejected because Conflicting application mode suffixes: '-AU' and '-ME' cannot both be appended. Table A4 standardizes exactly one application mode suffix per process designation.

results.query: How are the homograph AB and the position 2F disambiguated in AWS A3.0?
results.answer: In AWS A3.0M/A3.0:2020: 1. The designation 'AB' is an authentic homograph: in Table A1 (p. 69) and Clause 4 it designates adhesive bonding, whereas in Figure A6 (p. 79) it designates arc brazing. 2. The designation '2F' designates horizontal fillet welding: in plate welding, it represents linear fillet welding of test plates (Figure B18(B)); in pipe welding, it represents circumferential fillet welding of test pipes with pipe axis vertical (Figure B20(B)/(C)).

results.query: Compare the active process variation FCAW-G with the obsolete process atomic hydrogen welding (AHW) in AWS A3.0.
results.answer: Per AWS A3.0M/A3.0:2020, atomic hydrogen welding (letter designation: AHW) is an obsolete process classified in Table A5 (p. 74) and Annex D Table D4, whose definition is retained in Clause 4 for historical interpretation. In contrast, gas shielded flux cored arc welding (letter designation: FCAW-G) is an active standard process variation classified in Table A1 (p. 69) and Clause 4.
